append_decisions.evidence: Supplemental reference to the genuine additional defect discovered and repaired during successful native batch-55 Step3a adjudication; the original dispatched refuter decision remains unchanged. Focused current review confirms the added all-independent-P/Q-assignment finite-second-moment hypothesis is now in the opening Statement. For each of the finitely many section functions f_eta, sectionwise Cauchy–Schwarz bounds its squared integral under either first-coordinate law by the corresponding mixed kernel moment; the common (P+Q)-null-set prescription supplies simultaneous versions. Expanding g_t and then E_(tP+(1-t)Q)[g_t^2] gives finite polynomial coefficients times finite cross-integrals, proving the stated finiteness and continuity. Antisymmetry gives the zero pooled parameter and opposite projections. The old claim genuinely failed: for P=delta_0, Q density 3x^-4 on [1,infinity), h(x,y)=xy(x-y), its direct P-times-Q moment is zero but the pooled first projection mu_t*z^2-nu_t*z has infinite second moment because mu_t>0 and EQ^4=infinity. The native fatal classification and fixed disposition are therefore retained. Supplemental reference to the genuine additional defect discovered and repaired during successful native batch-55 Step3a adjudication; the original dispatched refuter decision remains unchanged. Focused current review confirms step 4.1 counts sample r-subsets and chosen coordinate slots jointly. A fixed a-subset of m observations extends to exactly binomial(m-a,r-a) r-subsets and is selected once in each; dividing by binomial(m,r) gives binomial(r,a)/binomial(m,a). The independent Y-block count multiplies it by binomial(r,b)/binomial(n,b), yielding exactly binomial(r,a)*binomial(r,b)*U_(a,b). The count includes a=0 or b=0. The old fixed-slot uniformity explanation was false (the first position of an increasing pair favors small indices) but the decomposition and coefficients remain correct. This supports the existing nonfatal fixed classification without altering its Statement.
